messages:
support-ops: Customer ACME (case 12345) reports their service endpoint acme-api.prod.svc is intermittently returning NXDOMAIN from their app nodes after a tenant network change. They can reproduce from a pod: `curl https://acme-api.prod.svc` -> `couldn't resolve host`. Can someone triage?

sasha: do we know whether this is node-local cache or upstream resolver? any quick dig output from a failing pod? also ask for VPC ID + whether they use resolver inbound endpoints / conditional forwarding.

support-ops: they ran `dig +short acme-api.prod.svc` inside pod -> nothing (NXDOMAIN). From host `dig` (host network) returns the private IP. They attached screenshots. VPC ID vpc-0a1b2c3d. No inbound endpoints configured on their account; they rely on our private hosted zone.

jamie: possible split-horizon: check Route53 private hosted zone is still associated with their VPC. Can someone run: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "acme-api.prod.svc"` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZZZ` (to inspect VPC associations).

carla: I asked the customer to run quick checks from a failing pod: `cat /etc/resolv.conf` and `dig +short acme-api.prod.svc @<node-local-ip>` and `dig +short acme-api.prod.svc @<vpc-resolver-ip>`

sasha: also ask them to check their egress allowlist / firewall. We recently saw a pattern where tenant network filters blocked UDP53/TCP53 to the VPC resolver and node-local returned NXDOMAIN.

support-ops: customer confirms node-local cache IP is `169.254.20.10` returning NXDOMAIN, host resolver (VPC+2) answers correctly. They also show a network policy that only allows outbound to a limited set of IPs — I suspect their egress firewall is blocking traffic from node-local to the VPC resolver.

jamie: that matches a past incident. steps: 1) ensure node-local can reach the VPC resolver on UDP/TCP 53 (usually VPC_CIDR_BASE+2). 2) if they have a forwarder/proxy, make sure it allows DNS over UDP/TCP to the resolver. 3) check NACLs/security-groups and any inline iptables on host. Commands they can run: `nc -vz -u <vpc-resolver-ip> 53` and `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53` from node-local pod/host.

infra-bot: deploy/route53-sync job completed 2026-03-16T08:12:10Z — no changes to hosted zones for vpc-0a1b2c3d.

carla: customer ran `nc -vz -u 10.0.0.2 53` and it times out. They have an egress appliance that only allows specific IP destinations; 10.0.0.2 was not on the allowlist.

sasha: yep that's the culprit. The node-local cache will forward to the VPC resolver; if that outbound path is blocked, node-local often returns NXDOMAIN quickly. Ask them to temporarily allow UDP/TCP to the resolver IP then test.

support-ops: asked customer to add 10.0.0.2 to egress allowlist and restart one failing pod to clear caches. Also suggested `kubectl exec -n kube-system -c node-local-dns <node-pod> -- kill -HUP 1` (or restart node-local daemonset) to flush DNS cache.

carla: after allowing 10.0.0.2 on egress, they report `dig +short acme-api.prod.svc` inside pod now returns the private IP. Pod-level app requests succeed.

jamie: add note to KB: when private hosted zone resolves only from VPC resolver, customers using node-local or stub resolvers must ensure outbound UDP/TCP port 53 to the VPC resolver IP (VPC base+2) is permitted by any egress filters. Also check for intermediate forwarders rewriting responses or TLS SNI inspection that can break EDNS.

support-ops: customer confirmed root cause = egress appliance blocking DNS to VPC resolver. Case closed (customer will add permanent rule). Thanks all :thumbsup:

carla: filing short postmortem note in case tracker with repro steps and suggested diagnostic commands.
